The detailed ONet15-1299.01 is Web Administrators, with tasks involving environment deployment and maintenance and website and application quality testing. US wages and employment use the Computer Occupations, All Other parent occupation and are not labeled as a separate administrator count.

Inputs include authorized website configuration, change records, logs, backup plans, and user problems; the access scope and data recipients are confirmed first, and being able to view logs does not mean logs may be published.

Tasks include fault diagnosis, patch updates, access control, monitoring, backup and recovery validation, content link updates, and testing; which ones you handle is verified against the position's division of work and authority.

Outputs are maintenance or change records, test results, backup and recovery notes, fault and user notifications, and quality improvement suggestions. A script or a screenshot of success is only partial evidence.

The operations and maintenance line focuses on environments, monitoring, changes, and recovery; the content quality line focuses on links, user feedback, and test results. The two lines may collaborate in one position, and the editorial classification does not prescribe manning.

Confirm problems, maintenance times, and impact with development, technical support, business, and users; record functions that remain unverified and do not use a fluent notification to conceal a fault.

The detailed ONet interests are CIE and Job Zone Four, which belongs to the US preparation framework; most related occupations require a bachelor's degree, but not all positions share a uniform education requirement. Employer requirements are verified against the actual notice, and a certificate does not grant system access.

ONet describes a controlled indoor setting, prolonged sitting, email and team communication, and time pressure; on-call duty and Chinese working hours are verified per position. W28 uses only fictional records and does not touch real accounts, logs, or systems.

Operations and maintenance and content quality are this occupation's two internal task types, and the success criteria must be specific to the environment, the check target, and the validation result.

How are maintenance and recovery distinguished from content checks?

Maintenance focuses on environments, services, and recovery; content checks focus on page links, feedback, and test results. The two need to collaborate, and one successful request does not prove all site functions or security, nor does it grant production operating authority.

Web administrators manage the design, deployment, development collaboration, and maintenance of website environments and carry out website and application testing and quality checks; specific tasks include fault diagnosis, updates and patches, backup and recovery, access permissions, log monitoring, content link maintenance, and user communication. The work must be done within the organization's authorized scope; being able to organize logs or write scripts does not mean you may change production systems or access user data.
Computer and information systems managers organize department resources, personnel, budgets, and projects, and website maintenance experience does not automatically confer management responsibility.
Search marketing strategists analyze query intent and marketing metrics and optimize impressions and conversions; website stability and quality are not marketing results themselves.
Computer systems analysts analyze business and application problems, system capabilities, and integration options, with a scope beyond website maintenance.
Information security analysts assess system risks and protective measures, and a web administrator reporting an anomaly does not mean being authorized to conduct independent vulnerability testing.

How do you choose between website maintenance and the adjacent occupations?
The first two rows are the maintenance and content quality internal tasks, and the last four are frozen adjacent occupations; compare the actual targets, outputs, and responsibilities.

If you like keeping records, locating problems, and continuous maintenance, look into operations and maintenance; if you prefer checking content and feedback, focus on quality checks. When turning to management, marketing, systems analysis, or security, build up the target preparation and authority.
The detailed ONet definitions of this occupation and the four neighbors support the differences; the selection signals are editorial suggestions, not a unified entry standard.
Then determine whether AI assists with organizing text, checking records, or operations that would affect real systems.

Generative text can help organize fictional check records, problem lists, and user notification drafts, which is an editorial use suggestion. Actual log times and versions, fault causes, and repair results still need to be checked, and recovery is not assumed complete just because an explanation reads well.

Monitoring, scripts, testing, and generative text each have their own tasks and inputs. The ONet software list does not measure an AI adoption rate; a script being able to run does not mean its output is correct or that you have production authority.

description.text: Learn about the website maintenance, backup and recovery, and quality testing tasks of web administrators, distinguish US Other Computer Occupations proxy data, related Chinese recruitment, and authority requirements, and complete the W28 fictional check record and the seven-day paper experience.

title.text: Web administrators: tasks, authority, and entry experience

subject.name: Web administrators
subject.summary: Web administrators manage the design, deployment, development collaboration, and maintenance of website environments and carry out website and application testing and quality checks; specific tasks include fault diagnosis, updates and patches, backup and recovery, access permissions, log monitoring, content link maintenance, and user communication. The work must be done within the organization's authorized scope; being able to organize logs or write scripts does not mean you may change production systems or access user data.
